outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua managed to put up decent numbers despite the Rams' dismal offensive performance in their season opener, and he'll look to ramp up his production further in Week 2 against the Giants. Nacua recorded 74 of Matthew Stafford's 155 passing yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco, though he caught just five of nine targets. No other Rams pass catcher had more than three catches or 26 yards, so there's little doubt that Nacua unsurprisingly remains Stafford's favorite target. The Giants' defense looked good in a win over Dallas in Week 1, with top wideout CeeDee Lamb posting a modest 5-44-1 receiving line.
outlooksByWeek.3: Puka Nacua (hip) is uncertain to play in the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Nacua missed Monday's Week 2 game versus the Giants, though he wasn't ruled out until game day. That lends some hope that Nacua could return soon, though his availability for practice during the week should provide more insight about his potential to return versus the Broncos. Should Nacua suit up, he'll draw a tough Denver secondary that have given up just 203 receiving yards to wideouts so far, tied for third-fewest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dontayvion Wicks made his presence felt in his Eagles debut in Week 1. Wicks reeled in two passes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the 24-22 win over Washington. Only Dallas Goedert had more receiving yards than Wicks for the game. Wicks also notched four targets in his premiere for the Birds. In Week 2, Wicks will face a dismal Titans defense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing scores a season ago, which was tied for 23rd in the NFL
outlooksByWeek.3: Dontayvion Wicks continues to cement himself as the No. 2 wideout in the Eagles offense. Wicks caught five passes for 74 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Wicks was second on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury, and with Dallas Goedert also banged up, Wicks could be one of the chief beneficiaries.

player.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kalif Raymond could continue to be a consistent option as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Raymond benefited from a high-scoring Week 1 win, reeling in eight of nine targets for 84 yards. The veteran wide receiver was also on the field for 60 percent of offensive snaps, so it appears at least a WR3 role is cemented moving forward. He'll face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points (55.2) to his position this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Woody Marks is set to occupy a change-of-pace role behind David Montgomery in Week 2, when the Texans host the Bengals. Marks turned 11 touches into 40 scrimmage yards in Week 1 against the Bills, while Montgomery had 79 yards and three TDs on 23 touches. Cincinnati had the worst run defense in the league last season, but Marks' modest usage makes him no better than a deep-league flex play as long as Montgomery is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Woody Marks capitalized on a negative game flow in Week 2, out-touching David Montgomery 13-8. The 0-2 Texans will face a Colts team that's also 0-2 in Week 3, and Montgomery is likely to reclaim the lead role unless Houston falls into a multi-score hole again. Marks is averaging just 2.9 yards per carry and 4.2 yards per catch in 2026 after averaging a modest 3.6 yards per carry during his 2025 rookie season. He has RB3/flex upside in Week 3 against a Colts defense that's giving up 177 rushing yards per game, but Marks' uncertain role and poor efficiency this season cap his value despite the intriguing matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Marks, a fourth-round NFL draft pick in 2025, played a substantial role as a rookie, soaking up 220 touches (22nd among RBs), but he struggled with efficiency (his 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 yards after contact both ranked near the basement) and found the end zone only five times. The result was 9.4 fantasy points per game and one top-10 fantasy outing. Marks appears ticketed for a lesser role in 2026 now that David Montgomery was brought in to serve as the likely leader of a backfield committee. Especially in an offense that doesn't use backs in the passing game very much, Marks is no more than a bench/insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker was perfect in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, connecting on all four of his extra points and converting his only field-goal attempt from 28 yards. The offense looked more potent with a healthy Patrick Mahomes under center, Kenneth Walker as the new bell-cow back, and a returning Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator, and Butker should see his opportunities rise if that trend holds. He could be busy in Week 2 against a Colts team that just got routed by the Ravens and was tied for 20th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field-goal attempt in the second quarter of Week 2, but he made up for it by converting the rest of his opportunities, including a 40-yard FG that gave Kansas City the overtime win over the Colts. The veteran kicker has been busy in the early going with six FG attempts and seven PATs, and a resurgent offense led by a healthy Patrick Mahomes and new bell-cow back Kenneth Walker should continue to supply Butker with volume. He'll face a Dolphins team in Week 3 that's giving up 31.0 points a game in the early going.

outlooksByWeek.2: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. St. Brown kicked off the season with a bang against the Saints, catching 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns. The star wide receiver continues to hold the monopoly in Detroit's passing game, and his production doesn't look to be taking a dip any time soon. He'll take on a Bills defense that ceded a seventh-most PPR points to Houston wide receivers (40.0) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. St. Brown finished with a monster performance in Week 2, bringing in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns. Not only has the star pass catcher recorded back-to-back two-TD performances, but he's also now amassed 19 catches for 209 yards in that stretch. He should continue to benefit from Detroit's shaky defense, even against a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.

player.seasonOutlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jeremiyah Love's second NFL game for the Cardinals will be a tough Week 2 matchup against Seattle. Love was largely held in check by the Chargers in Week 1, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and catching two passes for nine yards, but he did get into the end zone on a five-yard run. He logged six fewer carries and 20 fewer rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier, which isn't ideal for fantasy managers who drafted the rookie with the expectation that he'd be the lead back right off the bat. Even if Love gets a larger share of the workload against Seattle, he could struggle against a defense that held Patriots No. 1 RB Rhamondre Stevenson to 2.8 YPC in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jeremiyah Love is still looking for his first big breakout game heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash in San Francisco. Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Herbert struggled in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards and one touchdown with one interception, while adding 29 rushing yards on five carries. Injuries along the offensive line were once again an issue for the club; the interior of the line, with rookie Jake Slaughter at center, wasn't able to hold up, and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel didn't seem to have many answers. Ladd McConkey also suffered a rib injury in the game, which could make things even more difficult for Herbert if the top wideout misses any time. Herbert will look to rebound in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season with Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator. Through two games, he's completed less than 60% of his passes with a 2:3 TD:INT ratio and barely over 200 passing yards per game. Ladd McConkey was his only reliable target in the Chargers' opener, but the third-year wideout was limited by a rib injury in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and no one else stepped up. As in years past, Herbert's protection has also been decimated by injuries. An offensive line that was already missing starting center Tyler Biadasz was down to a third-string left guard against Las Vegas in Week 2, and the team also lost its two best blocking tight ends, Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, over the course of that contest. Herbert could be in for another long day in Week 3 against a Bills defense that has seven sacks through two games, tied for fourth in the league, but which has been vulnerable through the air when the opposing QB has found some time.

player.seasonOutlook: Herbert enters his seventh NFL season following a solid 2025 campaign in which he ranked just inside the top 10 quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns. Herbert added serious value with his legs, ranking fifth at the position in carries and second in rushing yards (career highs in both). He finished 10th among quarterbacks in fantasy points, but that's a bit misleading, as his inconsistent production led to five top-five weeks but no other finishes better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and 15th in fantasy points per game in each of the past four seasons, though it's fair to expect a leap forward in 2026 with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater healthy and a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel. Herbert is safest as a QB2, but there's upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026.
