Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season. Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery scored three total TDs in his Texans debut in Week 1 and profiles as a borderline fantasy RB1 for a Week 2 home game against a Bengals defense that gave up 93 scrimmage yards and a score to Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving. Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxson Dart was electric in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for an additional 54 yards in the stunning 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Dart threw just five incompletions and showed excellent rapport with new tight end Isaiah Likely. Dart was accurate, decisive and poised in what amounted to an extremely promising start to the season for the G-Men. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Los Angeles Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in their opener, allowing 379 scrimmage yards, which ranks them in the bottom third of the NFL. The Rams were torched on the ground in particular to the tune of 174 yards. While Myles Garrett will be sidelined due to a knee injury, the Rams will get Aaron Donald back from retirement when they host the Giants on Monday Night Football.

player.seasonOutlook: Dart is a strong 2026 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie campaign in which he delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for fifth most) despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. Dart was solid as a passer but elite as a rusher, finishing in the top five at the position in rushing attempts, yards, TDs and carries inside the 5-yard line. Dart's aggressive playing style raises concerns about his durability, but it also provides the 23-year-old with elite fantasy upside. With a new coaching staff led by John Harbaugh and a new playcaller in Matt Nagy, as well as an improved supporting cast that includes a healthy Malik Nabers and newcomers Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney, Dart is best valued as a midrange QB1 with a high ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the Cowboys for a Week 3 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on both PATs during Baltimore's 24-17 loss in Week 2. Loop's first attempt from 49 yards was blocked, but he followed up by making his second attempt from the same distance. He should have plenty of opportunities to score in what's expected to be a high-scoring contest versus Dallas inside the AT&T Stadium dome in Week 3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. The 30-year-old was Tampa Bay's second-most productive wideout in the Week 1 loss, hauling in all four of his targets for 40 yards. Godwin likely won't have many big plays after sustaining multiple serious lower-body injuries throughout his career, but he should remain a reliable PPR option and an important part of the Buccaneers' offense moving forward. Additionally, he's in for a great Week 2 matchup, as the Browns defense allowed 13.6 yards per target to WRs in Week 1, the second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Godwin is on the comeback trail after injuries have limited him to 16 games during the past two seasons. In 2025, he appeared in nine games and reached 11 fantasy points only twice. It seems like a long time ago, Godwin was second among receivers in fantasy points in 2024 when he suffered a severe ankle injury. He wasn't nearly as effective when he was on the field last season, but he's now more than a full year recovered from the injury and has less target competition with Mike Evans no longer on the roster. Entering his age-30 season, Godwin's days as a fantasy WR1 may be over, but with Emeka Egbuka as his only competition to lead the team in targets, he certainly has a path to flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will aim to stay perfect as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Santos was on the field a lot in Week 1 against the Panthers, but most of his 11 points came from his eight PATs. The veteran kicker could continue to benefit from a high-scoring offense, and he'll look to continue against a Minnesota squad that allowed three field goals and an extra point to Trey Smack this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cairo Santos will aim to do more as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Santos made his first field-goal attempt against the Vikings in Week 2, but his second chance for a tie was blocked in the fourth quarter. The veteran kicker's potential for the rest of the season remains up in the air following the injury to Caleb Williams, but an inexperienced Tyson Bagent could get the field-goal team on the field more often rather than finding the end zone. Philly has allowed 6.0 fantasy points per game to kickers this year, a top-10 mark in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Jefferson will look to keep it rolling in Week 2 as Minnesota takes on the Bears. Jefferson returned to a fantasy level in Week 1 that he didn't see much of in 2025, reeling in eight of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The star wideout also had a solid connection with veteran Carson Wentz, who came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion). Given that Jefferson still produced with the Vikings' QB2, he could be in line for big games no matter who lines up under center, so long as it isn't J.J. McCarthy. He'll face a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Jefferson will look to rebound from a quieter week as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jefferson was held to three catches for 55 yards against the Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in bad weather and ended with a 9-3 score. The superstar pass catcher has 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he could increase those numbers twofold against a Bucs defense that ceded 95 yards and a touchdown to Cleveland receiver Denzel Boston this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns aren't fully solved, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to work as the starter. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2.
