Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker didn't get many chances to hit the scoreboard in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, converting both his extra points but failing to see a field-goal attempt. The team's offense didn't quite look in sync yet under new coordinator Mike McDaniel, and top wideout Ladd McConkey was knocked out of the game early with a rib injury, so scoring drives could be tough to come by for the club in the short term. Dicker will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Raiders team that finished 25th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14.8 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite Carolina's defensive struggles, Young threw for 361 yards, the third-most in the NFL during Week 1, and led the offense to 37 points. Additionally, he added a touchdown on the ground as the Panthers offense looked more aggressive than in 2025. Young is also in for a favorable matchup, as he threw for 569 yards and accounted for four total touchdowns in two games versus the Falcons in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown won't suit up for at least four weeks for the Patriots, beginning in Week 2 against the Steelers, after landing on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins figure to be New England's top three wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets and a few carries, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kavontae Turpin managed just one catch for eight yards in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Turpin remains mostly utilized as a kick returner at this stage, though the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Williams' role could be elevated for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers with WR Omar Cooper (ankle) questionable. Williams logged just one Week 1 target despite playing 62% of the snaps in a game where the Jets led early and throughout-a script unlikely to materialize again in Week 2. With potential double-coverage on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell running vertically, Williams could find ample space underneath without Cooper's presence, making him someone to consider in very deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Williams will look to build on an expanding role in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. Elevated to No. 3 on the depth chart with Omar Cooper landing on IR, Williams recorded six targets last week, catching them all for just 34 yards. The Jets' offense is unlikely to score enough to sustain a third viable receiver, but if there were such a matchup, it would be Week 3 against a secondary that's already allowed 437 yards to wideouts through two games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook faces a challenge for fantasy managers in the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyjae Spears had five touches to Tony Pollard's eight in Tennessee's season-opening loss. Heading into a Week 2 home game against the Eagles, the Titans once again look like one of the NFL's worst offenses. Given Spears' role as a supporting piece in Tennessee's low-octane offense, he's tough to trust as anything more than a low-end deep-league flex play. Spears has exceeded 50 scrimmage yards three times in 14 appearances since the start of last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyjae Spears is likely to see a handful of touches as usual for the Titans behind Tony Pollard in Week 3, but that projected usage is enough for Spears to earn flex consideration in deeper formats against a Giants defense that has struggled to defend RBs. The Giants just allowed at least 92 scrimmage yards apiece to the Rams' backfield duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but the Rams boast one of the league's most talented offenses and led the league with 30.5 points per game last season, while the Titans are averaging 15.0 PPG after scoring 16.7 PPG last season. Spears can make big plays happen in space, as he showed in compiling 70 yards on nine touches in last week's loss to the Eagles, though he had just 24 yards on five touches in the season-opening loss to the Jets.

player.seasonOutlook: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Myers will look to remain perfect this season when the Seahawks visit Arizona in Week 2. Myers made his lone PAT try and both field-goal attempts in a season-opening win over New England, though his FGs were relative chip shots from 30 and 26 yards. Myers made nine field goals from 50-plus yards out each of the previous two seasons, however, so he has plenty of leg to convert from that distance when called upon. The Cardinals aren't expected to be a top NFL defense this year, but they performed well in limiting the Chargers to 14 points in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Myers has provided Seattle with a steady boot this season heading into a Week 3 matchup against Washington. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field-goal tries and all five of his PAT attempts through two weeks. However, he hasn't yet been asked to hit from distance, as none of his FG tries have been from 40 yards or greater. The Commanders have yielded a whopping 30.5 points per game through two weeks, so Myers could get plenty of opportunities to kick in Week 3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will look to remain a top target as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. LaPorta recorded six catches for 52 yards and his first touchdown of the season against the Bills in Week 2. The starting tight end has now been targeted 15 times across two games, and he's converted these into 11 grabs for 100 yards and a touchdown. He'll face a New York defense that held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to just two catches for 15 yards this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Williams' snaps could increase for the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Despite not drawing a target to open the season, Williams will likely ascend the depth chart following A.J. Brown's ankle injury that will sideline him for at least a month. Williams has shown big-play potential, so he may not require heavy volume to contribute, but until New England reveals its new receiving rotation, Williams can only be considered in the deepest of formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Williams hopes for more opportunities in Week 3 as the Patriots face the Jaguars. Rising up the depth chart with A.J. Brown on IR, Williams still only recorded a 21% snap share, registering two targets and a 10-yard catch in Week 2 where New England completed only 14 passes. Williams has big-play potential, but the passing game isn't operating at a high enough level to sustain a No. 4 WR despite facing a defense that's allowing 10.3 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams showed some flashes as a rookie, but he has a tough path to a Year 2 breakout. The 2025 third-round pick didn't see the field much (31% snap share), but he scored three touchdowns on 21 targets, all of which came from Week 10 on. He was utilized as a situational deep threat (17.6 aDOT), which led to a low catch rate (48%) but plenty of big plays (20.9 YPR). That role may not change much in 2026, as Williams will now compete with newcomers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, as well as incumbents DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for targets in a good New England offense led by Drake Maye. Unfortunately, he doesn't have a path to fantasy consistency and is best stashed only in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.
